timeouts.wait_timeout: ends only the caller wait and never cancels the operation
timeouts.operation_deadline: requests cancellation and normally ends Cancelled with reason deadline
timeouts.protocol_timeout: fails the operation in the controller error domain after a bounded handshake or ACK exchange
timeouts.transport_write_timeout: bounds partial report and command writes independently from protocol replies

operations.terminal_commit: exactly once; immutable result and error are mutually exclusive

terminal_transaction.child_admission: the parent cancellation node is sealed before owner cleanup; admission linearized after sealing is rejected and previously admitted children are cancelled
order: close and cancel the admitted cancellation subtree
commit one immutable terminal state and terminal event
terminal_transaction.failure_isolation: cancellation tree sealing transfers hook and child ownership without invoking hooks or dropping user captures while operation state, cancellation hooks, or children locks are held; hook invocation, discarded capture destruction, child ownership release, and panic payload destruction are isolated per item, so one fault never truncates sibling hooks or child propagation; event, registry, hook, reentrant destruction, or poisoned-lock faults never skip registry unlink or waiter notification

runtime.explicit_close: the only deterministic shutdown path; an external caller owns the Active to Closing transition and every concurrent or later caller receives the same saved Closed or Failed CloseOutcome
runtime.reentrant_close: a resource callback running on the deterministic close owner thread receives CloseOwner before waiting when it synchronously re-enters close on the same Runtime; the outer close continues to the one saved outcome
runtime.final_handle_drop: synchronously rejects admission and requests root cancellation only; it never waits, invokes resource close callbacks, joins tasks, spawns a finalizer thread, closes event production, or promises RuntimeClosed
runtime.supervised_tasks: tasks are created only through Runtime supervised spawn; Runtime registers before body execution, binds owner automatically, shares one consumable completion and JoinHandle ownership with the returned task handle, joins and unregisters, rejects same-Runtime synchronous close from the task before state changes, and lets explicit task join wait for TLS destructors and OS thread exit even after nondeterministic Runtime storage release
runtime.close_failure: resource, task, event, or registry failure commits CloseFailed with one saved diagnostic CloseReport, publishes runtime.close_failed as the final event, closes producers, and wakes all close waiters; operations whose owner cleanup or owner task has not finished remain non-terminal
close_order: publish RuntimeClosing and cancel the root tree
close resources in Runtime ID order while isolating each failure
wait for owner cleanup and join ordinary supervised tasks
finish non-terminal operations only after their owners exit
join internal workers and every retained task handle
verify operation, resource, active-task, and join registries are empty
save the Closed outcome, enter Closed, and notify close waiters

events.single_reader: each subscription admits one active reader; a concurrent reader fails immediately with ResourceBusy without consuming an event
events.overflow: oldest ordinary events are summarized by EventGap; authoritative state remains queryable
events.close: RuntimeClosed bypasses subscriber severity and log filters and is emitted only after successful cleanup, task join, and registry convergence; CloseFailed uses runtime.close_failed as the final event; either final event leaves subscriptions drainable and rejects later publish attempts; Drop alone emits neither final event

controller.report_interval_scope: every report, including cancellation and close neutralization
controller.direct_success_boundary: the complete report bytes were accepted by transport

sequence.origin: monotonic time when the command lane acquires the sequence
sequence.offsets: absolute from origin and monotonically non-decreasing
sequence.same_offset: apply in input order and emit one merged report
sequence.drift: targets never derive from the previous dispatch
sequence.cancel_or_failure: remove pending steps, accept a neutral report when connected, then release lease and commit terminal state

controller.automation_lease: exclusive arbitration primitive only; ECS is outside this milestone

classifications.rule: button, HAT, stick, handshake, and 7-bit report bytes match the audited source
sequence timing uses validated absolute monotonic offsets instead of the source constructor defect
cancellation and failure neutralize before terminal observation and lease release is observable
late ACK generations cannot complete a later request
